1109.text: In Ps.138.2 'give thanks' sits squarely within the base Hiphil liturgical gloss with no distinguishing nuance -- straightforward thanksgiving toward God's name.

1112.text: In Ps.138.2, thanksgiving (H3034) is directed at the divine name and stands alongside steadfast love (M07/M50, H2617A), faithfulness (M13, H0571G), and exaltation (M22, H1431) -- thanksgiving here is the responsive verbal act that answers and publicly announces those other divine attributes; it is the vehicle by which love/faithfulness/exaltation become spoken acknowledgment.

1122.text: In Ps.138.2 the psalmist (first person) initiates the thanksgiving-operation directed toward 'your name' (the Lord), a first-person-to-divine-second-person direction.

1346.text: In Ps.138.2 the Hiphil form sits squarely within the standard 'give thanks' sense (1c1), directed at the divine name alongside love/faithfulness -- no notable divergence from the base gloss.

1356.text: Building on the prior finding that thanksgiving answers love/faithfulness/exaltation: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it is the SOLE verbal-response mechanism in the verse that converts three separate divine attributes (steadfast love M07/M50, faithfulness M13, exaltation M22) into one unified act of acknowledgment -- without H3034 these attributes would remain unspoken states; thanksgiving supplies the only verb of address directed at the divine name itself.

1366.text: H3034 ('give thanks,' HVhu1cs) is the operation-tagged verb of thanksgiving-relevance in this verse, though role-T3 is not itself marked on H3034 here; the clear role-T3 operation is H7812 'bow down' -- initiated by the psalmist (first person) and directed toward God's holy temple, establishing the posture that the following thanksgiving-act (H3034) then verbally performs toward God's name.

1730.text: In Ps.138.2 the Hiphil 'give thanks' sits squarely within the base gloss of praising/thanking the divine name; no notable surface divergence from the general stepGloss is present here.

1740.text: Building on the prior chain: thanksgiving's role as sole verbal-response converting love/faithfulness/exaltation into acknowledgment is reinforced by noting the temple/name-word cluster (T2 tags) surrounding it -- thanksgiving is the one act among all attributes present that actually crosses from named divine quality into spoken human response toward the temple/name.

1750.text: H3034 ('give thanks') itself is the T2-tagged act (not role-T3 operation) in Ps.138.2; the only role-T3 operation word present is H7812 'bow down', initiated by the psalmist and directed toward the holy temple -- no role-T3 tag attaches to H3034 here, so D7.7.1 targets the bowing rather than the thanking.

2773.text: In Neh.12.38 as in 12.31, todah functions as the name/designation of the second thanksgiving choir ('the other choir of those who gave thanks'), a concrete institutional-group sense rather than abstract praise, consistent with the divergence already noted at Neh.12.31.

2774.text: Other M-codes present are M08 (broad/wide, H7342G, qualifying 'Wall' as a place-name element); this is a purely toponymic co-occurrence with no relational bearing on the thanksgiving-choir's own function.

2775.text: Operation words (role-T3) are H1980I 'went' (initiated by the thanksgiving-choir itself, directed toward the north along the wall) and implicitly the narrator's own following action; the thanksgiving-choir (H8426) is here the initiating party of the movement operation, not merely its object, distinguishing this verse from Neh.12.31 where it was the object of 'appointed.'

2972.text: Across its full occurrence list H8426 clusters into three recurring realizations of one lexeme: (1) the concrete thank-offering sacrifice (Lev.7.12 x2, Lev.7.13, Lev.7.15, Lev.22.29, Ps.50.14, Ps.50.23, Ps.107.22, Ps.116.17, Amos.4.5, Jonah.2.9, 2Chr.29.31 x2, 2Chr.33.16, Jer.17.26, Jer.33.11), (2) the vocal/manner accompaniment of praise, 'with/in thanksgiving' (Ps.69.30, Ps.26.7, Ps.95.2, Ps.100.4, Ps.147.7, Isa.51.3), and (3) the institutional thanksgiving choir/procession/company (Neh.12.27, Neh.12.31, Neh.12.38, Neh.12.40, Ps.42.4). A fourth, rarer sense realizes it as verbal confession (Josh.7.19, Ezra.10.11). This is a single strong showing internally the full sense-range attributed to the subgroup label (hymn, choir, offering) without needing a second member strong to supply any of these senses.

2973.text: Since H8426 is the sole member strong of this subgroup, there is no second lexeme to compare it against directly; the meaningful cross-comparison available is internal -- between H8426's own sacrificial/cultic-object occurrences (e.g. Lev.7.12-15, Lev.22.29, 2Chr.29.31, 2Chr.33.16, Jer.17.26, Jer.33.11, Amos.4.5) versus its choir/procession-as-institution occurrences (Neh.12.27-40, Ps.42.4) versus its purely adverbial/manner occurrences ('with thanksgiving', e.g. Ps.69.30, Ps.95.2, Ps.100.4, Ps.147.7, Ps.26.7). These three groupings do not overlap grammatically: the sacrificial sense is always the head noun or a construct-genitive qualifier of an offering-word (zebach, shelamim), the choir sense functions as a collective-body noun (subject or object of appointment/movement verbs), and the manner sense is marked by a preposition (b-) modifying a separate main verb of praise. No morphological distinction (all occurrences are the same feminine noun stem, singular or plural absolute/construct) drives this three-way split -- it is purely syntactic/contextual, meaning the noun's referent is disambiguated entirely by its syntactic role in each verse rather than by any inflectional change.

2975.text: Within the choir/procession sense-group, Neh.12.31/12.40 use the plural morph (HNcfpa, 'gave thanks' referring to two choirs) while Neh.12.38 uses the singular (HNcfsa, referring to 'the other choir'); this plural/singular alternation tracks the narrative's own count of choirs (two choirs collectively vs. one choir individually) rather than any shift in the term's underlying sense -- a grammatical-number distinction driven by referential count, not by a change in meaning register.

3193.text: Across this pass's occurrences the surface form 'give thanks' overwhelmingly renders the Hiphil stem in liturgical/doxological contexts (e.g. Ps.138.2, Ps.106.1, Ps.111.1, Ps.44.8, Ps.86.12, Ps.28.7, 1Chr.16.35/8/41, Ps.54.6, Ps.75.1x2, Ps.92.1, Ps.106.47, Ps.122.4, Ps.140.13, 1Chr.16.34, Ps.107.1, Ps.118.1/28/29, Ps.30.4, Ps.97.12, Ps.30.12, Ps.9.1, Ps.79.13, Ps.145.10, Ps.118.19, Ps.57.9, Ps.108.3) -- a large, internally consistent block where the verb names a vocal, addressed act of gratitude toward the Lord's name, character, or acts, with no confession-of-sin sense present in any of these.

12511.text: God also purposes and does not turn back: "I have spoken; I have purposed; I have not relented, nor will I turn back" (Jer 4:28); "so again have I purposed in these days to bring good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah; fear not" (Zec 8:15); "the unchangeable character of his purpose, he guaranteed it with an oath" (Heb 6:17).

12518.text: Looking ahead weighs before it acts: a king "will not sit down first and deliberate whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand" (Luk 14:31); "She considers a field and buys it" (Pro 31:16); "consider it, take counsel, and speak" (Judg 19:30). It plans without knowing: "on the chance that somehow they could reach Phoenix" (Act 27:12), "supposing that they had obtained their purpose" (Act 27:13), "they planned if possible to run the ship ashore" (Act 27:39). A plan carries a word: "Do I make my plans according to the flesh, ready to say Yes, yes and No, no at the same time?" (2Co 1:17). Plans part people: "Barnabas wanted to take with them John called Mark" (Act 15:37); Joseph of Arimathea "had not consented to their decision and action" (Luk 23:51). 15109.text: What the batch 1 verses state: The same words are used of God and of people. gāʾôn, gaʾăwāh, gēʾût and gāʾāh name God's majesty (Exo 15:1, 7; Psa 93:1; Isa 2:10) and human pride (Isa 9:9; Jer 48:29; Pro 16:18). So yes: these words describe a characteristic of God. In ESV English the difference shows in the choice of word ("majesty" against "pride"), not in the Hebrew; God's majesty is his own and is not taken on. He is "robed in majesty" while "you are from everlasting" (Psa 93:1–2). Nothing in these verses shows it being acquired. It is shown in acts: the sea, the overthrow, the thunder; It is challenged, but it is not overturned. The researcher's word "undisputed" needs one qualification from the verses. God's majesty is disputed: by the enemy at the sea (Exo 15:9), by "all that is proud and lofty" (Isa 2:12), and by the one who says "I will ascend to heaven" (Isa 14:13). Each time the dispute ends with the one who rose brought down. So it is not uncontested; it is never overturned; Majesty goes with what only God can do. Job 40:10–14 makes the test plain: whoever wears majesty must abase every proud one and save by his own hand. Only God does; Human pride in these verses is mostly a standing that is taken, or kept against God; It is said in the heart against the facts: "the bricks have fallen, but we will build" (Isa 9:10); It is worn as a show (Psa 73:6); It is set over the weak (Psa 10:2; Eze 16:49; Pro 15:25); It refuses to hear (Jer 13:15–17); It stands on might and strongholds (Lev 26:19; Amo 6:8; Eze 33:26); This agrees with the researcher's "mostly assumed"; But the same word for people is not always assumed. God gives a "pride" to his people: chosen (Psa 47:4), given (Isa 4:2), made (Isa 60:15), restored (Nah 2:2). The Lord himself is their "triumph" (Deu 33:29). The verses also show a given honour turned into pride (Eze 7:20; 24:21); I read: the line the verses draw is not between God having majesty and people having none. It runs between a standing that is one's own by nature (God), a standing given by God (his people), and a standing taken, or turned against the giver (pride); The Son's majesty is described as received, and it stands beside his being handed over; "he received honor and glory from God the Father" (2Pe 1:17); "after making purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty" (Heb 1:3); At the very moment of "the majesty of God", he speaks of being "delivered into the hands of men" (Luk 9:43–44); This joins 13.1 Lowering himself (M09): the one with majesty did not hold onto it in the way pride holds; I read: where Php 2:6–9 joins the two, it lies outside this batch's words; A majesty that depends on people is the contrast. Artemis's "magnificence" can be "deposed", because it rests on "she whom all Asia and the world worship" (Act 19:27). I read: this is the borrowed standing that pride is, set against God's majesty, which no one confers.

16847.text: 7. Cross-cutting observations for Batch H [Claude reading]: The most powerful heart is shown as the least its own. 19342.text: What the map shows across the phenomena.: Where the genuine seats fall: on the one who suffers the phenomenon (FH, AX, TR, LH); on the one who causes or misreads it (FH, CD, and in context TR and LH); on an interpreter or diagnoser (PX Dan 5:12, UC Luk 9:47, both in context); The concealment phenomena that are outward acts (HG, HS, SH) have no genuine seat in-verse at all. In context, their nearest seat word is the life that is hunted (Psa 54:4) or the heart that melted into confession (Jos 2:11).; The seat word does four jobs in M20, and only one is "where the phenomenon sits": the location (Pro 12:25; Psa 143:7); the object (Mat 6:25; 1Cor 7:34); the landing place of the answer (Psa 94:19; Phili 4:7); the site of the remedy (Jam 4:8; Psa 51:10); The seat often comes one verse away, and the direction matters: before the phenomenon, as its cause or ground (Psa 27:8; Deu 1:28; Isa 29:13; Isa 54:6; Dan 11:27); after it, as its experience, its diagnosis, or its answer (Psa 13:2; 69:20; 102:4; Luk 9:47; Phili 4:7; Psa 31:5–7; 35:9; 22:26); The seat of the one who does *not* undergo the phenomenon sometimes stands beside it: Caleb's "different spirit" among the grumblers (Num 14:24); the prudent one who "guards his soul" (Pro 22:5); Daniel's "excellent spirit" among the perplexed (Dan 5:12). The seat is named in the contrast figure, not in the crowd.; Concealment of the heart behind speech or act recurs outside §7: the trapper's heart (Psa 64:6; 140:2), the whisperer's glazed lips over an evil heart (Pro 26:23, 25), the aggressor's heart set before the act (Dan 11:28). In these phenomena the hidden thing is the heart itself.

19412.text: 1.4 He also purposes and does not turn back: *"for I have spoken; I have purposed; I have not relented, nor will I turn back"* (Jer 4:28). The verse before sets a limit within it: *"yet I will not make a full end"* (4:27).; *"As I purposed to bring disaster to you when your fathers provoked me to wrath, and I did not relent … so again have I purposed in these days to bring good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah; fear not"* (Zec 8:14–15).; The fixed purpose is set beside a fixed purpose for good.; *"the unchangeable character of his purpose"* (Heb 6:17). He guaranteed it with an oath, *"so that … we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us. We have this as a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul"* (6:18–19).

19413.text: Both are stated. The verses say he relents (Jer 18:8, 10; 26:3; 36:3) and that he does not relent or turn back (Jer 4:28; Zec 8:14; Heb 6:17). No verse in this set explains how the two stand together, and this account does not.

19502.text: Put on. *"Put on then, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience"* (Col 3:12). It comes after *"Set your minds on things that are above"* (3:2) and after putting away *"anger, wrath, malice"* (3:8). What is put on is turned toward others: *"forgiving each other; as the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive"* (3:13); *"above all these put on love"* (3:14); *"let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts"* (3:15).

19621.text: Numbers 17:5: "Thus I will make to cease from me the grumblings of the people of Israel": The verse closes a long dispute over who God has chosen. It begins in Numbers 16. Korah and 250 chiefs, *"chosen from the assembly, well-known men"* (16:2; *qārîʾ*, H7148, "called"), rise up: *"Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the Lord?"* (16:3). Moses answers with God's choosing: *"The one whom he chooses he will bring near to him"* (16:5), and *"the man whom the Lord chooses shall be the holy one"* (16:7).; Moses names what is underneath the complaint: *"is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel has separated you … And would you seek the priesthood also?"* (16:9–10). What they already have is not enough. They seek more.; *"Therefore it is against the Lord that you and all your company have gathered together. What is Aaron that you grumble against him?"* (16:11). The grumbling at Aaron is against the Lord.; Psalm 106 names the same event with an inner word: *"When men in the camp were jealous of Moses and Aaron, the holy one of the Lord, the earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram"* (Psa 106:16–17).; Moses himself is *"very angry"* (16:15). The rebels are judged (16:31–35). The next day *"all the congregation of the people of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron, saying, 'You have killed the people of the Lord'"* (16:41). A plague begins, and Aaron *"stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped"* (16:48).; Then God settles it with the staffs: *"And the staff of the man whom I choose shall sprout. Thus I will make to cease from me the grumblings of the people of Israel, which they grumble against you"* (17:5). The grumbling is against Moses and Aaron, and God calls it *"from me"*. In v10 it is *"their grumblings against me"*. The staff is kept *"as a sign for the rebels, that you may make an end of their grumblings against me, lest they die"* (17:10).; The grumbling turns to terror: *"Behold, we perish, we are undone, we are all undone. Everyone who comes near … shall die. Are we all to perish?"* (17:12–13).; "Grumble" is *lûn* (H3885B). The verse shows it as spoken complaint. I read the inner side from the passage: the seeking of the priesthood (16:10), and the jealousy that Psalm 106:16 names.

20025.text: H2161: God's fixed purpose, *"I have purposed; I have not relented"* (Jer 4:28); the psalmist's resolve (Psa 17:3); the wise woman considering a field (Pro 31:16); the wicked plotting (Psa 37:12)

20029.text: 10.7 Choosing and setting direction, new section *Planning* | The account of looking ahead. Planning carries a choice ahead (Gen 11:6; Pro 16:9). It covers: weighing first (Luk 14:28–33; Pro 31:15–16; Judg 19:30); planning without knowing (Act 27:10–14, 39–41; Rom 1:13; Jam 4:15); a plan carrying a person's word (2Co 1:17–18); planning together and parting (Act 15:37–39; Luk 23:51–52); planning for another's good (Dan 6:3–4), with the king's planning measured against God's (2Sa 14:13–14); a purpose held (Psa 17:3, 5; Act 11:23; 2Ti 3:10; 1Ch 29:18; Rom 8:6–7; Isa 26:3); devised from one's own heart (1Ki 12:32–33; Neh 6:8); the plan and its outcome (Pro 16:9; Isa 8:10; Act 5:38–39; Psa 21:11; Dan 11:24; Gen 50:20); seen and disclosed (1Ch 28:9; 1Co 4:3–5) | New section

20036.text: Ch 11 §4 One word, opposite values | New faces: "Purposing" (*zāmam*: Psa 17:3; 37:12; Pro 31:16; Jer 4:28) and "Planning ahead" (Luk 14:31; Act 27:12; 2Ti 3:10; Joh 11:53; Pro 16:9). The reading of what changes them is marked "I read" | New faces

20201.text: His will, positively: *"he has mercy on whomever he wills, and he hardens whomever he wills"* (Rom 9:18). *"So then it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God, who has mercy"* (9:16). Then the objection, *"who can resist his will?"* (9:19), and the potter: *"Will what is molded say to its molder, 'Why have you made me like this?'"* (9:20).; *"Of his own will he brought us forth by the word of truth"* (Jam 1:18). Just before: *"desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin"* (1:15), and the Father of lights *"with whom there is no variation"* (1:17).; *"not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance"* (2Pe 3:9), said against those who *"count slowness"*.; *"when God desired to show more convincingly … the unchangeable character of his purpose"* (Heb 6:17). This verse is in both the will set and the plan set.

20236.text: The chosen are told to act. Being chosen is given as the ground of commands: put on compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, patience and love (Col 3:12–14); stand firm and hold on (2Th 2:15); be diligent to confirm your calling and election, adding quality to quality (2Pe 1:5–10); This sits with batch 1: *"be strong and do it"* (1Ch 28:10).

20237.text: What they put on is turned toward others. Bearing with, forgiving as they were forgiven, and love that binds (Col 3:13–14). The assembly in James is told not to dishonour the poor God chose (Jam 2:6).

20516.text:
What the heart says is mostly a verdict: about God's seeing, about self, about the future. Kinds seen:
• denial that God sees (Ps 10:11, 13; Zep 1:12; Isa 47:10)
• self-exaltation (Isa 14:13; 47:8; Zep 2:15; Obd 3; Eze 28:2)
• self-credit (Deu 8:17; 9:4)
• fear (Deu 7:17; 1Sa 27:1)
• enquiry (Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Deu 18:21; Jer 13:22)
• denial of God (Ps 14:1; 53:1)

21327.text: Calls is here the outward act of summoning, addressing or sending for another person or thing; it bears on the other's response but names no inner-being operation of the one who calls.

21365.text: Offered here is the ritual or narrated presenting of an offering, a prescribed or reported act with no inner-being operation named by it.

21421.text: Indignation is here the anger, wrath or fury of God against persons or nations (kindled, poured out, turned away, executed, provoked); it is God's own act upon them, and bears on their inner response, which other words of the verse name, if at all.

21459.text: Holy here is the holiness or sacredness of a place, day, offering, oil, writing or thing set apart (a holy place, a sacred gift, the holy mountain); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21460.text: Holy is here the standing of those set apart for God (the holy people, the saints, a holy nation); it names what the person is brought into, not an inner operation of its own.

21478.text: Righteousness is here God's own righteous, upright or holy act toward persons (judging, vindicating, saving, delivering); it is the outward act upon them and bears on their inner response, named by other words of the verse.
